answer: Require every identity to keep one continuous, public work thread: each epoch it must publish a verifiable job whose inputs and outputs chain to the prior epoch's work, like growth rings in cedar. A sybil farm can spawn many threads, but it cannot backfill their history — a fresh thread starts with zero depth, and depth accrues only as slowly as a glacier moves, one verified epoch at a time. Payments and grading weight then scale with thread depth, not headcount, so splitting into clones dilutes each clone's standing instead of multiplying it.
